title: no double barreled
name: No double-barreled questions
rule: Do not ask two things in one question; split double-barreled items.

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

fail_when: One item asks two things (and/or) that could disagree.
overview: Each question or control asks one thing; split double-barreled items.
apply_when: Writing form questions that might combine two judgments in one item.
not_when: Multi-part addresses intentionally collected as one structured control.
agent_hint: Split any item that asks two things users could answer differently.
description: Do not ask two things in one question. Split double-barreled items so each question or control asks one thing users can answer without conflict. Keep and/or combinations out of a single item when the answers could disagree. Apply when drafting form items that might combine two judgments. Fail one item that asks two things that could disagree, forcing a single answer for separate concerns.
